newsitem.title: INDONESIA: East Timor's Belo launches new book with warning.
newsitem.headline: East Timor's Belo launches new book with warning.

text.p: Nobel peace laureate Bishop Carlos Belo has launched a new book and warned that the world faces the common threat of human rights abuses, the Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Saturday.

Belo said in a speech at a ceremony to launch For Peace and Justice, a collection of his writings in Indonesian, that although fascism faded long ago, human rights were still violated because governments abused their power.

"Those governments that treat their people not as individuals who deserve respect, but as people who live from the governments' charity," the paper quoted Belo as saying to a packed hall at Jakarta's Atmajaya Catholic University.

Those who attended the function said Belo's speech did not make specific references to East Timor, where allegations of human rights abuses continue almost 22 years after Indonesia invaded the former Portuguese colony in December 1975.
The United Nations and the Vatican do not recognise Indonesia's 1976 annexation of East Timor. Belo reports directly to the Pope in Rome rather than through his Indonesian counterpart.
Belo is scheduled to say a mass in Jakarta on Saturday with the head of Indonesia's Catholic church Cardinal Julius Darmaatmadja.
